seen: One row per decade of the seasonal transform: a yearly wave, about eleven per row, with a fast fuzz riding on it. The fuzz is thicker in some rows and thinner in others (rows 2, 4, 6 look thinner in their second halves). Nameable at once: a beat, every year, and a fuzz that swells and shrinks. That the beat is yearly needs the caption; that it repeats does not.

The same yearly beat as V20, but the rank scale has pushed the line against the top and bottom of each row: flat plateaus, a blocky square-ish wave, and the thin/thick contrast between rows made far starker than in V20. It looks clipped, but N0.3 is not quite it: nothing is cut off. What is wrong is that the contrast is the scale's, not the material's. No norm I hold said that, so N2 is written now.

Raw values, rank scale, one row per decade. Each row sits at a different height inside its band: high in the 1970s, falling through the 1990s, low in the 2000s, and the 2020s hugging the floor. That is the slow story of the day's length (my belief L1, recognised, not encountered). But the eye has to reassemble it across seven rows: the layout cuts one slow arc into seven segments. The yearly beat is there too, weaker. Failure is the cut, not the scale; N2 also applies, less. N3 written now.

Strip, tidal, linear: a woven cloth of blue and red with diagonal hatching. At first look a texture, so N0.1 fails it. A second look found what the first did not: pale horizontal bands where the hatching nearly vanishes, recurring down the page at roughly equal spacing (around rows 7-9, 17-19, 27-29 counted by eye; not measured). That is not on my list of beliefs (L3 names tidal terms, not a slow swelling of them). The diagonals I cannot tell apart from a beat between the tidal period and the calendar grid (N0.2). Fails at thirty seconds; the bands are kept as a note for V20's thick and thin rows, which may be the same thing.

V19 with a linear scale. The amplitudes are now honest (N2 is satisfied) and the slow story is almost gone: each row's height inside its band shifts by a little, the 1990s row visibly sinks, and nothing else of the decadal arc reads. The yearly beat and the fast fuzz show, quieter than V20. Fails on N3, written two variants ago: the slow movement is cut into seven pieces, and here the pieces are too small even to reassemble.

Strip, seasonal, rank. One shape at once: a dark blue column down the middle of every year (roughly days 150-250 by the pixel position, so northern summer), red on both sides, the red split into two lobes. Recognition of L2 (the seasonal cycle), and the two lobes look like the semi-annual term. Two norms speak against it and I overrule both. N0.4: nothing tells a stranger which way time runs, but the shape does not need time's direction, only the year's. N2: the rank scale sharpens the edge of the blue column, but it does not make the column; the place of the shape is the material's even if its contrast is the scale's. N4 written now to say where N2 stops.

V10 with a rank scale: the same woven cloth, more saturated, and the pale bands that V10's second look found are mostly gone. Rank flattened the swelling of the tidal amplitude, which is the only shape V10 had. A texture at thirty seconds (N0.1), and N2 in its plain sense: the scale erased the material's amplitude.

Spiral, seasonal, linear: a disc, blue in its lower half (the summer side, since January stands at twelve o'clock), red above. The seasonal shape is there. But the first thing the eye takes is optical: moire rings and spokes near the centre, and a seam running straight up from the hole where each year joins the next. That is the renderer's structure competing with the material's (N0.2). And the outer years look paler than the inner ones only because their dots are spread over a longer circumference: the layout gives later years more room and less ink. No norm said that; N5 written now, not decisive here.

Line, tidal, linear, the whole sixty-four years left to right. It looks like the waveform of a sound: a dark mass that swells and narrows, four swells across the width, the narrow waists at roughly a third, a half-and-a-bit and four fifths of the way along (by eye). A stranger says 'it breathes' within seconds. This is the thing V10's pale bands and V20's thick and thin rows were glimpses of: the size of the fast tidal wobble itself swells and shrinks on a period of very roughly eighteen or nineteen years, by eye. Not on my list of beliefs. An encounter, and it arrived at a variant made by a grid, not by a decision.

Spiral, raw, rank. A red heart and a blue rim, like the cross-section of a trunk: the early years (inside) long days, the recent years (outside) short. The slow story reads in one radial sweep, so N3 is met where V18 and V19 failed it, and N4 admits the rank scale because the colour's place is what matters. N0.1 says it works. But N5, written one variant ago, says what is wrong: the rim, which is the recent and most surprising part (the shortest days), is drawn in sparse dots and looks faint, while the heart is dense. The two norms pull apart and I cannot decide. Unsure, held back by N5.

Strip, raw, linear. Horizontal bands: deep red across the upper third, a pale band, red again, then blue down to a dark blue floor in the last rows; a faint lighter column in mid-year behind it. The slow story reads in one downward sweep (N3 met), every year gets the same ink (N5 met), and N0.1 says works. It is the clearest picture of the slow movement so far, and I wanted to pass it. N0.4 stops it, and here it bites where at V09 I overruled it: V09's shape was a season and did not need time's direction; this shape is a trend and does. Nothing on the page says whether red is the past or the future. A prior norm decided against my liking.

V04 with a rank scale. The four swells are still there, but the mass now fills the frame from edge to edge and the waists are shallow. What V04 showed is an amplitude, the size of the wobble growing and shrinking, and rank is the one scale that flattens amplitude. N2, written at V21, decides it in its plain sense.
